reason: The cited evidence shows laser cladding of HEA+WC composites on steel (E2) and general benefits of laser cladding (E8), but no passage directly supports the key premises that this specific intervention suppresses hot cracking, refines microstructure, or improves properties over fusion-weld repairs on crack-prone substrates. The evidence is only loosely related to the core claims.
premises: Laser cladding refines microstructure and reduces residual stresses via rapid solidification
WC particles reinforce the coating and suppress crack initiation/propagation
The HEA composite coating is dense, fine-grained, and crack-resistant
The coating improves hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance relative to fusion-weld repairs and untreated surfaces
The approach is applicable to substrates prone to hot cracking under high thermal input
